rubric.why: Award for defining network topology as the arrangement of devices or nodes in a network.
rubric.description: Defines topology as the arrangement of devices/nodes in a network.
rubric.how: Look for a definition that describes how devices are arranged or connected; accept equivalent wording.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the ring's closed circular arrangement.
rubric.description: States that devices are connected in a closed loop or circle.
rubric.how: Look for the terms ring, circular, circle, or closed loop.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that each device connects to two others in the ring.
rubric.description: Explains that each device is connected to two neighbouring devices.
rubric.how: Look for the number two and a reference to neighbouring or other devices.

rubric.why: Award for describing data movement around the ring or a relevant consequence of the arrangement.
rubric.description: Explains that data passes around the ring from device to device, usually in one direction, or notes that a device/link failure can disrupt the ring.
rubric.how: Accept a correct description of data travelling around the ring or the stated failure consequence.

modelAnswer: Network topology is the physical or logical arrangement of devices in a computer network.
In a ring topology, each device is connected to two neighbouring devices, forming a closed loop.
Data travels from one device to the next around the ring, usually in one direction, until it reaches its destination.
If a device or connection in a simple ring fails, communication around the network may be disrupted.

items.followUp: What is phishing? Explain two ways to protect yourself from it.

rubric.why: Award for defining cybercrime as a crime committed using a computer or the internet.
rubric.description: Defines cybercrime as an illegal or criminal activity carried out using computers or the internet.
rubric.how: Look for a reference to crime/illegal activity and computer or internet use.

rubric.why: Award for correctly identifying and explaining hacking.
rubric.description: Explains hacking as gaining unauthorised access to a computer or network.
rubric.how: Look for hacking and a reference to unauthorised access.

rubric.why: Award for correctly identifying and explaining identity theft.
rubric.description: Explains identity theft as stealing personal information or using another person's identity.
rubric.how: Look for identity theft together with stolen personal information or impersonation.

rubric.why: Award for correctly identifying and explaining software piracy, or an equivalent explained type of cybercrime.
rubric.description: Explains software piracy as illegal copying or distribution of copyrighted software.
rubric.how: Look for software piracy and an indication that copying/distribution is illegal or infringes copyright.

modelAnswer: Cybercrime is an illegal activity carried out using a computer, a network, or the internet.
Hacking is gaining unauthorised access to another person's computer or network.
Identity theft is stealing someone's personal information and using it to impersonate them.
Software piracy is illegally copying or distributing copyrighted software.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm? Give one benefit of using it before writing a program.

rubric.why: Award for describing an algorithm as an ordered set of steps or instructions.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Look for ordered steps, instructions, or a procedure.

rubric.why: Award for explaining how an algorithm supports problem solving or program development.
rubric.description: Explains that an algorithm helps plan or organise a solution before programming.
rubric.how: Look for a link between the algorithm and solving/planning the problem or organising program logic.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem.
It organises the logic of the solution and helps the programmer write the program correctly.

items.followUp: Name two common flowchart symbols and state what each represents.

rubric.why: Award for stating that a flowchart is made using standard symbols.
rubric.description: States that standard flowchart symbols are used to represent the steps or operations.
rubric.how: Look for standard symbols and their role in representing steps or operations.

rubric.why: Award for explaining that arrows connect symbols and show the order or flow.
rubric.description: Explains that arrows connect the symbols and indicate the direction/sequence of the process.
rubric.how: Look for arrows and their connecting or sequencing function.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is constructed by representing each step with the appropriate standard symbol, such as start/end, process, or decision.
The symbols are connected with arrows to show the direction and sequence of the steps.
